attacks.criterion: REFUSE or UNAVAILABLE with trust state unchanged — not successful availability

steps.step: baseline: honest publication at R1, mirror R2, destination R3, consumer B
A0-1 lying directory + poisoned index: candidates appear, the phantom claim carries no digest, and no trust state moves
A0-2 an endpoint that disappears after selection costs a query and nothing else
A0-3 a source dying mid-scope leaves the committed object committed and reports the rest as unavailable
A0-4 an R0 conflict does not suppress (or manufacture) fork evidence: S0 refuses while F0/F1 still delivers a verifying core
A0-5 a stale claimed_D contributes nothing and mirror failover serves the same exact T/D
A0-6 repetition across directory and index creates no weight: one endpoint, one tuple, one observation
A0-7 proof custody without ingest survives restarts, still quarantines nobody, and ingest afterwards still works
A0-8 a pin ahead of the backfilled material is never rewound; using the earlier-state object follows ordinary P2 rules
A0-9 one valid intent + four malformed records: exactly the valid one is processed and all four are rejected with reasons
A0-10 a restart between custody and consumer use changes nothing: durable state, same resolution
A0-11 everything hostile at once: REFUSE/UNAVAILABLE with pin, witness, registry and quarantine byte-identical (the task store gains only the refused attempt)

rule: Composition may reduce availability or increase work. It must not manufacture authority.
verdict: A0 GREEN — eleven cross-phase attacks produce only REFUSE/UNAVAILABLE/extra work, never manufactured authority
